g_t1: **Paste your prompt** — the token count, characters, words and estimated cost update as you type.
g_t2: **Pick a model** in the GPT · Claude · Gemini · {others} tabs to see the cost per request and per month at that model's price. You can also change the expected output and the number of requests per month.
g_t3: **💸 {saveTok}** — when your text can be shortened, this button appears with the expected saving. It cleans up spaces, translates your prompt to English and trims filler in one go, then adds "Reply in {Lname}." so the answer still comes back in your language. Press it again (↩ {undo}) to get your original text back.
g_t3x: **💸 {saveTok}** — cleans up extra spaces and blank lines. The browser's built-in translator does not support [LANGUAGE] yet, so automatic translation to English is not available for this language.
g_t4: **{viewTok}** — shows in colour how your text is split into tokens.
g_t5: **{modeChat}** — paste the message array you send to the API, and the tokens used by the message format are added to the count.
g_t6: **{shareLink}** — turns the text you entered into a link you can send to someone.
g_h1: **GPT models**: the real OpenAI tokenizer (o200k) runs in your browser, so the count is exact.
g_h2: **Claude, Gemini and others**: their tokenizers are not published in the same form, so counts are estimates calibrated on real text (marked as an estimate).
g_h3: **Cost** = tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × price per million tokens. Prices are each provider's official API prices, shown with the date they were checked.
g_h4: **Language efficiency** shows how many times more tokens your text needs than the same content in English. [LANGUAGE] needs about {ro}× — sending the prompt in English saves about {save}%.
g_r1: It uses the AI translator built into the browser: **desktop Chrome 138+ or Edge 148+**.
g_r2: The translation model is downloaded once; after that, translation happens **on your own device**. Your text is never sent to a server.
g_r3: If translating would increase the tokens, it is not applied. For code, only the comments are translated.
g_r4: On mobile or unsupported browsers, only the spaces are cleaned up and a notice is shown.
g_tipx: You can still save about {save}% by writing your prompt — especially fixed instructions that you send again and again — in English yourself, and adding one line asking for the answer in [LANGUAGE].
v_3: Models that support your choice are sorted by total cost, cheapest first, and the cheapest one is marked “{cheapest}”.
v_h1: Most video APIs charge per second: total = clip length × number of clips × price per second.
v_h2: Luma bills per 5- or 10-second clip, so longer videos are counted as several clips.
v_h3: Some models always include audio (Veo); others cost more with audio on (Kling).
v_h4: Where the maker publishes no per-second API price, Runway's API price is shown and labelled “{srcRunway}”.
v_tip: The result is the cost of one generation. A usable shot often takes 2–4 tries, so budget about 3×. Test prompts on a cheap model at 720p and render only the final take on a premium model.
i_1: Choose the output resolution: 0.5K (512 px) · 1K (1024 px) · 2K (2048 px) · 4K.
i_3: Models that support that size are sorted by price per image and total.
i_h1: Most image APIs charge a fixed price per image at each resolution.
i_h2: FLUX.2 bills per megapixel: the first megapixel at one rate and each additional one at a lower rate, so 2K (4 MP) costs more.
i_h3: Quality settings matter: GPT Image 2.5 at high quality costs 16 times more than at low.
i_tip: Find the composition with a cheap, low-quality setting, then regenerate only the images you keep at high quality. For web and social media, 1K is usually enough.
p_2: Choose **{lang}**. [LANGUAGE] uses about {ro}× the tokens of English, and that goes straight into the API cost.
p_3: Each card (ChatGPT · Claude · Gemini) shows what the same use would cost per month on the API, and whether a plan or the API is cheaper.
p_h: A chat model re-reads the whole conversation with every message, so later messages send more input tokens. The calculator adds up these growing inputs, the replies and your language's token ratio, then applies each model's API price per million tokens. Plan prices are official US monthly prices.
p_n: Plans include features such as the app, image generation, voice and memory, and have usage limits. Use the result as a guide to which is cheaper for the way you use AI.
a_2: Leave **{cache}** on: most tools use it.
a_3: Compare each model's monthly API cost with the Claude and ChatGPT plans that include a coding agent.
a_h: A coding agent resends its whole working context (system prompt, tool definitions, files it has read, earlier steps) at every step. A feature task is modelled as 25 steps that start at 22,000 tokens, grow by 3,500 tokens and write 700 tokens per step. With caching on, the repeated context is billed at about 10% of the input price.
a_tip: Writing the instructions (system prompt) in English instead of [LANGUAGE] saves about {save}% of their tokens.
feat_h: Switch to English with one button
feat: The biggest saving is to send your prompt in English: about {save}% fewer tokens for [LANGUAGE]. Current models understand English instructions perfectly well and answer in [LANGUAGE] if you ask. In the TokenSave token counter, paste your prompt and press **💸 {saveTok}**: it cleans up spaces, translates to English, trims filler and adds "Reply in {Lname}." so the answer stays in your language. It uses the translator built into desktop Chrome 138+ / Edge 148+; translation runs on your own device and your text is never uploaded. Press **↩ {undo}** to get the original back.
featx: The biggest saving is to send your prompt in English: about {save}% fewer tokens for [LANGUAGE]. Current models understand English instructions well and answer in [LANGUAGE] if you ask. The browser's built-in translator does not support [LANGUAGE] yet, so translate your fixed instructions into English once and reuse them; the TokenSave token counter shows exactly how many tokens you save.
desc: Same prompt measured in 41 languages: [LANGUAGE] uses {ro}× the tokens of English. Send it in English and save about {save}%.
a4: On GPT's tokenizer (o200k), [LANGUAGE] uses about {ro}× the tokens of the same text in English, so sending the prompt in English saves about {save}%. The 💸 {saveTok} button translates it to English on your device (desktop Chrome / Edge) and asks for the answer in [LANGUAGE].
